question: What does the box do to a plain lowercase word, a capitalized word, a word with spaces, and a word with digits/symbols — does it transform case, strip characters, reverse, encode, or return input unchanged?
expect: If outputs equal inputs, f is identity (or near-identity). If case changes consistently, it's a case transform. If spaces/digits/symbols are removed or altered, that reveals stripping/filtering. If order reverses, it's a reversal. Comparing the 10 varied strings pins down the basic per-character vs whole-string behavior before probing further.

question: Does the last-character shift wrap around the alphabet (y->a, z->b) or saturate/behave differently, and does it apply to the last character of the original string even when the inserted '2' moves things?
expect: If wrap-around holds, expect '2a', '2b', 'a2a', 'a2b', 'b2a', 'b2b', 'sk2a', 'fr2a', 'jaz2b', 'qui2b' (insert 2 at len//2, last letter +2 with wrap). If instead it saturates or uses a different rule, outputs will differ (e.g., 'y'->'a' vs 'y'->'y', or non-letter results), revealing whether the shift is modular and case-preserving. This pins down the only untested part of the current model on ordinary short words.

question: Does the +2 shift apply to the last character when it is a digit or symbol, and does the insert position use floor(len/2) for even-length strings ending in non-letters — tested on ordinary mixed alphanumeric/symbol strings.
expect: Model v1 predicts: abc1->ab2c1 (insert at 2, last '1' digit unchanged), abcd1->ab2cd1 (insert at 2, last digit unchanged), ab12->ab212 (insert at 2, last '2' unchanged), a1b2->a12b2 (insert at 1, last digit unchanged), cat9->ca2t9, dog!->do2g!, x1->2x1? (len2, insert at 1 -> x21? wait len2//2=1 -> x|2|1 = x21, last '1' unchanged), xy1->x2y1, '1'->21 (len1 insert at 0), '12'->1 22? (len2 insert at 1 -> 1|2|2 = 122, last '2' unchanged). If outputs differ, it reveals whether digits/symbols at the end are shifted, and whether insert position truly is floor(len/2) for even lengths. This pins down the two remaining ambiguities in the model on ordinary inputs.

question: Does the inserted '2' position depend on floor(len/2) even when the string contains multibyte/whitespace-only content, and does the +2 shift apply to the last character when it is an uppercase letter at the end of a mixed string?
expect: Predictions: 'Hi there' len8 -> floor 4 -> 'Hi t2here'? wait: H,i,space,t,h,e,r,e -> insert at 4: 'Hi t2here', last e+2=g -> 'Hi t2herg'. 'ABC def' len7 -> floor3 -> 'ABC2 def', last f+2=h -> 'ABC2 deh'. 'Zz' len2 -> p1 -> 'Z2z', last z+2=b -> 'Z2b'. 'Hello World!' len12 -> p6 -> 'Hello 2World!', last ! unchanged -> 'Hello 2World!'. 'aB' len2 -> p1 -> 'a2B', last B+2=D -> 'a2D'. 'AB' len2 -> p1 -> 'A2B', last B+2=D -> 'A2D'. '  ' len2 -> p1 -> ' 2 ', last space unchanged -> ' 2 '. 'a' len1 -> p0 -> '2a'. 'A' len1 -> p0 -> '2A'. 'cat Dog' len7 -> p3 -> 'cat2 Dog', last g+2=i -> 'cat2 Doi'. If all match, confirms insert position and last-char shift are independent of whitespace/mixed case; any deviation (e.g., shift skipping uppercase, or spaces affecting position) would reveal a hidden rule.

question: Does the +2 shift apply to the last character when it is a letter at the end of a string whose length makes the inserted '2' land right before that letter, and does the insert position stay floor(len/2) for longer ordinary sentences with punctuation?
expect: Model v1 predicts: the quick brown fox (len19, insert at 9) -> 'the quick2 brown fox' with x+2=z -> 'the quick2 brown foz'; Hello, World! (len13, insert at 6) -> 'Hello,2 World!' last '!' unchanged; abcde (len5, insert 2) -> 'ab2cde' last e+2=g -> 'ab2cdg'; abcdef (len6, insert 3) -> 'abc2def' last f+2=h -> 'abc2deh'; a b (len3, insert1) -> 'a2 b' last b+2=d -> 'a2 d'; ab c (len4, insert2) -> 'ab2 c' last c+2=e -> 'ab2 e'; cat (len3, insert1) -> 'c2at' last t+2=v -> 'c2av'; cats (len4, insert2) -> 'ca2ts' last s+2=u -> 'ca2tu'; dog. (len4, insert2) -> 'do2g.' last '.' unchanged; dog! -> 'do2g!'. If all match, it confirms floor(len/2) insertion and letter-only +2 shift on ordinary sentence-like inputs; any mismatch (e.g. insertion position or shift applying to punctuation) would reveal a different rule.

question: Does the inserted '2' go before or after the middle character when the string length is odd, and does the +2 shift still apply to the final letter — tested on ordinary short words where floor(len/2) vs ceil(len/2) would differ?
expect: Model v1 predicts floor(len/2): cat->c2av, dog->do2g?, apple->app2le (len5, pos2 -> ap2ple, last e+2=g => ap2plg), house->hou2se (len5 pos2 -> ho2use, last e+2=g => ho2usg), water->wa2ter (len5 pos2 -> wa2ter, last r+2=t => wa2tet), seven->se2ven (len5 pos2 -> se2ven, last n+2=p => se2vep), orange->ora2nge (len6 pos3 -> ora2nge, last e+2=g => ora2ngg), banana->ban2ana (len6 pos3 -> ban2ana, last a+2=c => ban2anc), elephant->elep2hant (len8 pos4 -> elep2hant, last t+2=v => elep2hanv), computer->comp2uter (len8 pos4 -> comp2uter, last r+2=t => comp2utet). If observed matches floor predictions, the model is confirmed on ordinary words; if the '2' lands one position later (ceil), the insert rule is wrong and needs fixing. This is the most common ordinary input type (plain lowercase words), and it directly tests insert position on odd lengths where floor vs ceil diverge.

question: Does the +2 shift apply to the last character when it is a letter that is also the character right before the inserted '2' position (i.e., when the insert lands after the final letter), and does the shift still apply when the last char is a letter but the string length is 1 or 2?
expect: Predictions: ab->a2c? Let's compute with model: len2, p=1 -> a|2|b -> a2b, last b+2=d -> a2d. abc len3 p=1 -> a|2|bc -> a2bc, last c+2=e -> a2be. abcd len4 p=2 -> ab|2|cd -> ab2cd, last d+2=f -> ab2cf. abcde len5 p=2 -> ab|2|cde -> ab2cde, last e+2=g -> ab2cdg. a len1 p=0 -> 2a, last a+2=c -> 2c. question: Does the +2 shift apply to the last character when the string ends in a letter but has an even length (so the inserted '2' lands mid-string), and does the shift wrap correctly at the alphabet boundary for ordinary words ending in y or z?
expect: Predicted: happy->hap2py? no: len5, p=2 -> ha|2|ppy -> ha2ppy, last y+2=a -> ha2ppa. lazy len4 p=2 -> la|2|zy -> la2zy, last y+2=a -> la2za. buzz len4 -> bu2zz, last z+2=b -> bu2zb. fizz -> fi2zz -> fi2zb. day len3 p=1 -> d|2|ay -> d2ay, last y+2=a -> d2aa. key -> k2ey -> k2ea. boy -> b2oy -> b2oa. toy -> t2oy -> t2oa. city len4 -> ci2ty -> ci2ta. baby len4 -> ba2by -> ba2ba. If outputs match, confirms wrap y->a, z->b on last char and floor(len/2) insert for even lengths ending in letters; any deviation reveals a different wrap or shift rule.

question: Does the +2 shift on the final letter wrap correctly for uppercase letters at the alphabet boundary (Y->A, Z->B), and does the insert position stay floor(len/2) for ordinary capitalized words and short phrases ending in uppercase Y or Z?
expect: If wrapping is plain +2 within case: Y->A, Z->B, AY->A2A, AZ->A2B, BY->B2A, BZ->B2B, SKY->SK2A, FRY->FR2A, JAZZ->JA2ZB, QUIZ->QU2ZB. If uppercase does NOT wrap (saturates or behaves differently), outputs will differ at Y/Z endings; this tells us whether the shift rule is uniform across cases or special-cases the boundary, which matters for ordinary capitalized words ending in Y or Z.
